changes.before: Change new Session(12) to new Session(). What happens?
changes.after: Set a new object's starting data with a constructor.

before: A constructor has the class name and no return type. new Session(12) passes 12 into that constructor. this refers to the object being initialized.
In this.minutes = minutes, this.minutes names the field and the bare minutes names the parameter. Assigning the parameter to itself would not initialize the field as intended.
Once this class declares Session(int), Java does not also generate a no-argument constructor. A new Session() call therefore needs a separately declared matching constructor.

Expected output or behavior: 12
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Add an explicit Session() that delegates with this(5), after consulting constructor-delegation syntax. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A constructor runs when an object is created. It has the class's name and no return type. Here, new Session passes a minutes input to the constructor. this means the object being prepared.
The constructor's input and the object's field are both named minutes. this.minutes names the field; minutes alone names the input. The assignment copies the input into the field.

Java supplies a no-input constructor only when a class declares no constructors. Session declares a constructor that needs an int, so a creation call must provide that input unless another matching constructor is added.
The program prints 12. The constructor stored its input in session.minutes before main read that field.
The quiz removes the input from new Session. Check which constructors the class actually declares.

before.question: Change new Session(12) to new Session(). What happens?
choices: Compilation fails: no matching no-argument constructor
The int constructor is skipped and an object appears
before.explanation: Only Session(int) is declared. Java does not synthesize the default no-argument constructor when another constructor is written.

after.question: Change new Session(12) to new Session(). What happens?
choices: Compilation fails because there is no no-input constructor.
Java skips the declared constructor and creates the object anyway.
after.explanation: The only declared constructor needs an int. Java does not add a no-input constructor beside it.
